title: Blessed days for Muslims
intro: Four chosen days in the year that Muslims celebrate.

learn.html: The blessed days (mubarak days) are four chosen dates in the year that Muslims mark in a special way, with worship and celebrations. We get ready to welcome them, and we take part in family, jama‘ah and community events.

learn.text: In the Hijri calendar the blessed days are:

items.label: 2. Mawlid – the birth of Muhammad (SAW) – 12 Rabi‘ al-Awwal

items: The Islamic New Year remembers the Hijrah – the move of Muhammad (SAW) and the Muslims from Makkah to Madinah in 622. Since then Muslims count their years by the Hijri calendar.
Mawlid is the day Muhammad (SAW) was born. It is marked by reciting the mawlid and other programmes.
Eid al-Fitr comes after Ramadan – the joy of having fasted and done our duties in Ramadan.
Eid al-Adha is the joy of Hajj, the qurbani and the takbirs of tashriq, hoping for Allah’s mercy and reward.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Besides these four blessed days, Muslims also mark four blessed nights.
